subject: Renewal and mid-contract expansion: pricing scenarios for Cordelia.ai
messages:
From: Alex Chu <ach@cordelia.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@cordelia.ai
Date: 2026-06-26T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Options for renewal + mid-year capacity increase

Hi Michael,

Our renewal is scheduled for Sept 1 and we're anticipating a meaningful uptick in inference usage starting in late July as we ramp a new feature. Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide: 1) pricing for a mid-contract top-up (prorated) that won't lock us into a larger annual commit, 2) a co-term path so everything lines up with Sept 1, and 3) an example of trade-offs if we convert to a reserved pool vs. pay-as-you-go.

They also asked for: one-page comparison and an estimated timeline for approvals (they need to know if PO/net-terms impact pricing).

I've attached the last three months of usage and our current contract export (current_usage_report.csv). Can you send options this week?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chu
Head of Platform
Cordelia.ai
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Options for renewal + mid-year capacity increase (Cordelia)

Team — forwarding Cordelia's ask. Quick read: customer wants mid-contract top-up options, co-terming, and a reserved-pool vs PAYG comparison. I sketched three scenarios in the attached matrix (renewal_scenarios_v2.xlsx):

- Scenario 1 — Short-term top-up: prorated add-on at near-list rate, one-time onboarding credit to offset integration friction.
- Scenario 2 — Co-term annualize: customer commits to an annualized higher base (12 months) with a blended discount; partial proration on the remainder of this contract.
- Scenario 3 — Reserved burst pool: 6-12 month reserved capacity with a discount + SLA uplift and guaranteed burst buffer.

Questions for you: Lauren — what discount banding should we show for Scenario 2 (we'll need an approval floor)? Ben — are there any SLA/priority constraints if we offer a reserved pool mid-cycle? Priyom — anything on procurement cadence (DocuSign vs PO lead times) that affects pricing?

Want to get this to Alex with a clean one-page comparison and a draft SOW tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Michael

--

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Options for renewal + mid-year capacity increase (Cordelia)

Michael — quick notes after a skim of the matrix:

- I would avoid a flat 25% off list on Scenario 2 unless they're committing materially (>=25% lift). Instead, propose a tiered discount: 8% at +15% commit, 12% at +25%, 16% at +40% (annualized). That lets us protect margin and incentivize higher commits.
- For Scenario 1 (top-up), include a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to ~1 week of usage) but price the top-up at list-prorated to avoid precedent.
- Scenario 3 (reserved pool) looks fine but add an SLA uplift clause (+P0 routing) and an early-termination fee pro-rated over the reserve term.
- Procurement note: Cordelia historically requires a PO and legal redlines take ~10 business days. If they need net-60 instead of net-30, we'll need finance sign-off (impact on discount).

I'll draft the discount language and redline the SOW (small changes) — loop me on the DocuSign link.

Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chu <ach@cordelia.ai>, contracts@cordelia.ai
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + expansion: 3 options and next steps (Cordelia.ai)

Alex — thanks for the quick context. Per our internal review (see Lauren's notes below), we've put together three concise options so you can present a single-page comparison to procurement. Attached: renewal_scenarios_v2.xlsx and a draft SOW (SOW-draft-Cordelia.pdf).

High-level options (numbers illustrative; final line-item pricing in the matrix):

1) Top-up (low-friction) — Mid-contract prorated add-on at list rates. No change to renew date. We offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to ~1 week of estimated usage to smooth integration. Minimal legal work; PO is sufficient.

2) Co-term + annualize (recommended if you want predictable unit economics) — Convert the remainder of current term into an annualized commitment (effective Sept 1) with tiered discounts: 8% @ +15% commit, 12% @ +25% commit, 16% @ +40% commit. Pro-ration applied to align to Sept 1; we can provide a blended monthly invoice. Requires DocuSign and standard redlines; procurement timelines apply.

3) Reserved pool (high-availability) — 6-12 month reserved capacity with an 18% discount and guaranteed burst buffer + SLA upgrade. This option includes a short early-termination pro-rate. Best for sustained high-throughput features. Finance will need to approve net-terms if you request >30 days.

Next steps: tell us which option you'd like pricing locked for so we can generate a final commercial and DocuSign package. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the matrix.
